/-!
# Minimum Overlap Problem

The minimum overlap problem asks for the limit of the minimum, over all
splittings of $\{1, \ldots, 2n\}$ into two sets $A$ and $B$ of equal size, of
the maximum number of representations of any integer $k$ as $a - b$ with
$a \in A$, $b \in B$, divided by $n$.

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_overlap_problem)

This file points to the canonical formalization in `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«36»`.
-/

reformulations.difference: The canonical definition imported by this redirect takes a natural-number supremum over all integer differences, whereas Wikipedia restricts k to the interval from −2n to 2n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any splitting of {1,…,2n}, both elements of every counted pair lie in that interval, so their difference lies in [−2n,2n]. All additional differences contribute zero. Overlap counts are bounded by the cardinality of A × B, so the natural-number supremum is genuine and equals the finite maximum over Wikipedia's interval. This equality and its induced equivalence for specifying the maximum were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.
